summary: Draft integrates most interim-note evidence well (crosswalk numbers, 1998 Ipsos nested panel, Casacuberta-Hardt separation, ecolRxC 565 datasets, SOE 175 elections, Marble & Clinton -60%). No critical/thesis-level failures. Gaps concentrate in the second-tour matrices section (§4) and a few dropped quantitative anchors. The single clearest omission is the vague 6 / vague 7 intention-vs-behaviour gap, which the parent explicitly flagged and which the draft ignores entirely.

findings.location: Section 4.A, paragraph beginning "Ce comportement de barrage se réutilise mal" (draft line ~114), and the second-tour matrices paragraph at end of §4 (line ~130)
findings.issue: The draft uses the 2024 front-républicain transfer figures (97 % NFP→Ensemble/LR, 73 % Ensemble→NFP) as if they were stable behavioural coefficients, and never surfaces the intention-vs-behaviour gap that the interim note treats as a first-order caveat. A campaign tool relying on POLL-BASED (i.e. declared-intention) transfer matrices needs this warning: declared pre-election intention systematically understates the actual second-round barrage.
findings.evidence: interim-report-matrices-front-republicain-reutilisation-2027 ("What the corpus already said"): CEVIPOF/Ipsos vague 6 (pre-2nd-round INTENTION) for the RN-NFP duel gave 41 % RN / 32 % NFP / 23 % abstention, versus vague 7 (post-2nd-round BEHAVIOUR) 97 %/73 %. The note calls this "un écart intention/comportement à l'intérieur même de la famille Ipsos, avant de parler d'érosion dans le temps" and lists it as an open question: is the vague 6/vague 7 gap "généralisable comme facteur de correction?" Sources [[rsultats-du-premier-tour-des-lgislatives-2024]] (CEVIPOF) and [[un-front-rpublicain-efficace-mais-illusoire-fondation-jean-jaurs]].
findings.recommendation: In §4.A add a sentence noting that declared pre-election intention (vague 6: 41 % RN / 32 % NFP / 23 % abstention in the RN-NFP duel) diverges sharply from measured post-election behaviour (vague 7: 97 %/73 %), within the same Ipsos family — so any 2027 second-tour matrix built on pre-election polls is a lower bound on the real barrage, and this intention-vs-behaviour delta is itself a candidate correction factor.

findings.location: Section 4, final paragraph on second-tour matrices (draft line ~130), around "un effet type de scrutin (législative→présidentielle). Ce dernier n'est plus hypothétique"
findings.issue: The draft asserts the type-of-election effect (législative→présidentielle) is real by pointing only to the forward-looking Elabe 2027 matrix. It drops the interim note's cleaner, independent empirical demonstration: a real presidential transfer matrix (2022) showing the type-of-scrutin effect is of the SAME order of magnitude as 20 months of temporal erosion. This is the interim's headline synthesis and it is the only true présidentielle-type ground-truth matrix available for a within-family comparison.
findings.evidence: interim-report-matrices-front-republicain-reutilisation-2027 ("What the new sources say" + "Evidence synthesis"): 2022 presidential exit matrix [[second-tour-profil-des-abstentionnistes-et-sociologie-des-lectorats-ipsos]] shows 1st-round Mélenchon voters transferring only 42 % to Macron (17 % Le Pen, 41 % abstention) vs two-thirds barrage in 2017; Pécresse (LR) 53 % to Macron. The note concludes: "à l'intérieur même de la source Ipsos, le changement de type de scrutin produit un écart comparable à celui produit par 20 mois d'érosion politique."
findings.recommendation: Add the 2022 presidential numbers (Mélenchon→Macron 42 %, Pécresse→Macron 53 %, vs two-thirds in 2017) as an independent anchor for the type-of-scrutin effect, and state explicitly that within a single pollster family the scrutin-type gap ≈ the 20-month temporal-erosion gap — which is why the matrix must be scenario-parameterised from a présidentielle source, not carried over from législatives 2024.

findings.location: Section 1.B (draft lines ~19-21) and Section 2.D/E where interval non-coverage is argued
findings.issue: The draft grounds its 'classement not pourcentage' thesis on coverage percentages (28 % MRP, 30-53 % EI) and on the theoretical Casacuberta-Hardt separation, but omits the one direct precinct-scale empirical demonstration that point precision and interval calibration DECOUPLE — the exact mechanism the thesis rests on. Adding it turns a theoretical claim into an empirically anchored one.
findings.evidence: interim-report-sophistication-vs-degradation-maille-fine ("What the new sources say"): [[putting-ecological-inference-to-the-test-part-1]] (Data for Progress, MA-7, SBC on real precinct data) finds EI point estimates hold as well as or better than the individual baseline while the posterior is overdispersed (S-shaped rank statistics) — "la première preuve directe... d'un DÉCOUPLAGE entre précision ponctuelle et calibration de l'incertitude à l'échelle infra-district."
findings.recommendation: In §1.B or §2.E, cite the Data for Progress SBC precinct test as direct empirical evidence that a point estimate can stay accurate while its credible interval collapses — the concrete counterpart to the Casacuberta-Hardt theory and the reason publishing a rank is defensible where publishing a percentage-with-interval is not.

findings.location: Section 5.B (draft line ~142), "résorbés par une cascade de règles jusqu'à ~98,9 %"
findings.issue: The draft compresses the REU↔MIOM reconciliation into 'une cascade de règles' without the actual tiers, even though the parent explicitly named 'cascade de règles REU' as exploitable detail and Axis 2 of the query asks specifically about INSEE/data.gouv crosswalks. The tiered breakdown is what makes the reconciliation reproducible rather than a black box.
findings.evidence: interim-report-crosswalk-bureaux-fiabilite ("What the new sources say", [[traitement-adresses-reudocmethodologiehtml-at-main-inseefrlabtraitement-adresses]]): (1) classic join on {code_commune}_{code_bv} ~66k/69k; (2) Paris/Lyon/Marseille arrondissement rules +~1.6k; (3) auto-association of single-bureau communes +~400; (4) manual eyeballing of renumbering patterns +~300; residual ~130 REU-side / ~250 SIE-side (~0.2-0.4 %), concentrated in Belfort, Troyes, Dieppe.
findings.recommendation: Expand the cascade into its four deterministic tiers with the counts (66k classic join → +1.6k PLM arrondissement rules → +400 single-bureau communes → +300 manual renumbering-pattern matches), plus the residual split (~130 REU / ~250 SIE) — so the reader sees how the 98.9 % is actually reached and where the irreducible failures sit.

findings.location: Section 2.H (downsian argument, draft line ~82) and/or Section 5.D (covariables)
findings.issue: The draft's pivotal downsian argument — that the actual local result beats demographic composition as a predictor — is made abstractly. The interim carries a French quantitative demonstration that composition genuinely does NOT exhaust RN geography, which is precisely the empirical warrant for that argument, but the draft never cites it.
findings.evidence: interim-report-implementation-bureau-ei-et-covariables ("What the new sources say", Bouba-Olga note): commune-level regression with regional fixed effects shrinks the raw rural/urban RN gap from ~11 points to 1.3-3.0 points net, R²=0.72, but leaves an unexplained regional residual from +12.7 points (PACA) to -8.8 points (Bretagne) — "preuve que la composition socio-démo n'épuise pas la géographie du vote RN." Source [[note-mthodologique-concernant-larticle-vote-rn-ce-qui]] / [[ce-qui-explique-vraiment-les-diffrences-de-vote-rn-entre-les-villes-et-les-campa]].
findings.recommendation: Add the Bouba-Olga residual (regional term +12.7 PACA to -8.8 Bretagne after socio-demographic controls, R²=0.72) as French empirical evidence that demographics leave a large unexplained geographic residual — directly justifying why the real 2024 bureau result, not its demographic composition, is the load-bearing covariate.

findings.location: Section 4.B (draft line ~120), "la corrélation au niveau circonscription entre européennes et législatives 2024 est de 0,89 pour la gauche"
findings.issue: The draft cites the headline 0.89 but drops the per-component breakdown, which is load-bearing for the question of WHICH blocs' spatial structure is transferable. The spread shows transferability is not uniform across the left — a directly relevant nuance for a composite baseline.
findings.evidence: interim-report-baseline-election-source-2027 ("What the new sources say", [[note-de-recherche-2]] CEVIPOF): the 0.89 overall left correlation decomposes to 0.42 for the PC ("structure en affaiblissement"), 0.86 for LFI, 0.82 for Verts — and the note stresses that no equivalent coefficient exists for RN/droite radicale, calling that "un vrai trou."
findings.recommendation: Append the component spread (PC 0.42, LFI 0.86, Verts 0.82) and note that the transferability of a scrutin's spatial structure varies by bloc (a weakening component like the PC transfers poorly), reinforcing why the missing RN/droite equivalent is exactly the backtest #3 the draft already proposes in §7.C.
